newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SANDVIK SEES HIGHER '97 OPERATING PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: SANDVIK SEES HIGHER '97 OPERATING PROFIT.

text.p: Swedish toolmaker Sandvik AB said on Tuesday it expected operating profits to be 500 million crowns higher in 1997 than a year ago.
The company said earlier its profit after financial items would be unchanged.
Managing director Clas Ake Hedstrom said the company had seen a strong trend in the country's economy in the first half of the year.

"We see an improving trend in the economy and our forecast is for a stronger operating profit but an unchanged profit after financial items," Hedstrom told Reuters after the company released its six month results.

"If you estimate that we had positive financial net income of 344 million crowns in 1996 and it is negative this year then this accounts for a difference in operating profit of about 500 million crowns."
In 1996 the operating profit was 4.11 billion crowns.
"We are seeing an upturn in Europe and most importantly in Germany, where we have had a positive development for a couple of months," he said.
"In Britain it had been a bit weaker while France is more difficult to estimate."
